narrative.title: The Backup Generator Split Test
narrative.scenario: A datacenter splits its battery cells between two backup racks. Site policy requires the heavier rack to outweigh the lighter one by exactly d kilowatt-hours — no other gap qualifies. The facilities engineer counts how many ways the cells can be assigned while honoring the precise power differential.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n, a difference d, and an array arr of n non-negative integers.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of partitions into subsets S1, S2 with S1 >= S2 and sum(S1) - sum(S2) = d, modulo 10^9 + 7.

testCases.explanation: Pick any two cells for the heavy rack and the last for the light one — three ways, gap 1 each time.

hintLevels: Level 1: If S1 - S2 = d and S1 + S2 = total, then S1 must equal (total + d) / 2.
Level 2: The task collapses to counting subsets that reach (total + d) / 2 — reuse the count-subsets DP.
Level 3: If total + d is odd or d exceeds the total, no split exists; answer 0 without running the DP.
